title: Activation of the Nrf2/ARE Pathway Attenuates BDE-47-Induced Immunotoxicity in RAW264.7 Macrophages.
authors: Gao, Qian; Deng, Qingyuan; Yang, Ziying; Wei, Lili; Chen, Hongmei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究BDE-47诱导巨噬细胞免疫毒性的Nrf2/ARE通路保护机制，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是毒理学与细胞实验，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), widely used as brominated flame retardants, are known to exert persistent adverse effects on the immune systems of humans and other organisms. Previous studies have demonstrated that 2,2',4,4'-tetrabromodiphenyl ether (BDE-47), a prevalent congener, induces apoptosis, impairs phagocytic function, and triggers aberrant immune-inflammatory reactions in RAW264.7 macrophages via the induction of elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. The nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/antioxidant response element (Nrf2/ARE) signaling pathway is a key cellular defense system against oxidative stress. In this study, we investigated the role of the Nrf2/ARE pathway in BDE-47-induced macrophage immunotoxicity. Network toxicology analysis identified Nrf2 as a hub gene within the BDE-47-associated immunotoxicity network. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested a potential interaction between BDE-47 and the Keap1-Nrf2 complex, with moderate binding affinity. Experimental studies in RAW264.7 cells showed that BDE-47 exposure activated the Nrf2/ARE pathway, as evidenced by Nrf2 nuclear translocation and the differential upregulation of downstream genes (GCLC, GCLM, HO-1, NQO1, SOD1, and CAT). Importantly, Nrf2 knockdown via lentiviral shRNA or pharmacological inhibition with brusatol significantly exacerbated BDE-47-induced apoptosis and immune dysfunction, including enhanced pro-inflammatory cytokine production and impaired phagocytosis. These results demonstrate that Nrf2/ARE pathway activation represents an adaptive antioxidant response and contributes to limiting BDE-47-induced cytotoxicity and immune impairment in macrophages.
abstract_zh: 多溴联苯醚（PBDEs）作为溴化阻燃剂被广泛使用，已知对人类及其他生物的免疫系统产生持续性不良影响。既往研究表明，2,2',4,4'-四溴联苯醚（BDE-47）作为一种常见同系物，通过诱导细胞内活性氧（ROS）水平升高，在RAW264.7巨噬细胞中引发细胞凋亡、损害吞噬功能，并触发异常免疫炎症反应。然而，其潜在调控机制尚不清楚。核因子E2相关因子2/抗氧化反应元件（Nrf2/ARE）信号通路是细胞对抗氧化应激的关键防御系统。在本研究中，我们探讨了Nrf2/ARE通路在BDE-47诱导的巨噬细胞免疫毒性中的作用。网络毒理学分析将Nrf2鉴定为BDE-47相关免疫毒性网络中的枢纽基因。分子对接和分子动力学模拟提示BDE-47与Keap1-Nrf2复合物之间存在潜在相互作用，且结合亲和力适中。RAW264.7细胞实验表明，BDE-47暴露激活了Nrf2/ARE通路，表现为Nrf2核转位及下游基因（GCLC、GCLM、HO-1、NQO1、SOD1和CAT）的差异性上调。重要的是，通过慢病毒shRNA敲低Nrf2或使用brusatol进行药理学抑制，显著加剧了BDE-47诱导的细胞凋亡和免疫功能障碍，包括促炎细胞因子产生增强和吞噬功能受损。这些结果表明，Nrf2/ARE通路激活代表一种适应性抗氧化反应，并有助于限制BDE-47诱导的巨噬细胞细胞毒性和免疫损伤。
